  hcpcs_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of HCPCS codes used in numerator, denominator, or exclusion criteria.']
  health_equity_focus boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this measure is prioritized for health equity analysis and disparity reduction initiatives.']
  higher_score_interpretation varchar [note: 'Indicates whether a higher measure score represents better performance, worse performance, or is not applicable.']
  icd10_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ICD-10 diagnosis codes used in numerator, denominator, or exclusion criteria.']
  last_updated_date date [note: 'Date when the measure specification was last revised or updated.']
  loinc_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of LOINC codes for laboratory tests and clinical observations used in measure specifications.']
  lookback_period_months varchar [note: 'Number of months prior to the measurement period during which historical data is evaluated for measure compliance.']
  measurement_period_end_date date [note: 'Ending date of the period during which measure performance is evaluated.']
  measurement_period_type varchar [note: 'Type of time period over which the measure is evaluated (calendar year, rolling 12 months, measurement year, or custom).']
  medical_record_review_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether manual medical record review is required as part of the hybrid data collection methodology.']
  minimum_denominator_size varchar [note: 'Minimum number of eligible members required in the denominator for the measure to be reportable and statistically valid.']
  name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the quality measure (e.g., Controlling High Blood Pressure, Comprehensive Diabetes Care).']
  ndc_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of NDC codes for specific drug products used in measure specifications.']
  nqf_number varchar [note: 'Four-digit identifier assigned by the National Quality Forum for endorsed quality measures.']
  numerator_definition varchar [note: 'Detailed specification of the criteria that members must meet to be included in the numerator (compliant population).']
  numerator_exclusions varchar [note: 'Criteria for removing members from the numerator even if they initially met numerator criteria.']
  place_of_service_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of two-digit codes identifying the location where services were rendered for measure evaluation.']
  product_line_applicability varchar [note: 'Lines of business to which the measure applies (e.g., Commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, Marketplace).']
  quality_improvement_priority varchar [note: 'Internal priority level assigned to this measure for quality improvement initiatives and resource allocation.']
  regulatory_agency varchar [note: 'Name of the regulatory agency to which this measure must be reported (e.g., CMS, State Department of Insurance).']
  regulatory_reporting_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this measure must be reported to state or federal regulatory agencies.']
  reporting_deadline_date date [note: 'Date by which measure results must be submitted to regulatory or accreditation bodies.']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'How often the measure results must be calculated and reported to regulatory bodies or internal stakeholders.']
  retirement_date date [note: 'Date when this measure was or will be retired and no longer used for quality reporting.']
  revenue_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of UB-04 revenue codes used to identify specific services or accommodations in measure specifications.']
  risk_adjustment_method varchar [note: 'Statistical methodology used to adjust measure results for differences in patient case mix or severity.']
  rxnorm_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of RxNorm codes for medications used in numerator, denominator, or exclusion criteria.']
  sample_size_required varchar [note: 'Number of medical records that must be reviewed for hybrid measures to meet NCQA sampling requirements.']
  score_type varchar [note: 'Type of calculation used to express measure performance (proportion, ratio, continuous variable, or rate).']
  social_determinants_of_health_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this measure incorporates or is influenced by social determinants of health factors.']
  stars_rating_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this measure is included in the CMS Stars rating program for Medicare Advantage and Part D plans.']
  stars_rating_domain varchar [note: 'CMS Stars rating category to which this measure contributes (e.g., Staying Healthy, Managing Chronic Conditions, Member Experience).']
  stars_rating_weight decimal(3,2) [note: 'Weighting factor applied to this measure in the overall CMS Stars rating calculation (typically 1, 3, or 5).']
  status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the measure (active, retired, under development, suspended, or deprecated).']
  steward varchar [note: 'Organization responsible for developing and maintaining the measure (e.g., NCQA, CMS, NQF).']
  stratification_criteria varchar [note: 'Specific dimensions by which measure results must be stratified (e.g., age groups, gender, race/ethnicity, disease severity).']
  stratification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the measure must be reported with stratified results by demographic or clinical subgroups.']
  subcategory varchar [note: 'More granular classification within the measure category (e.g., Diabetes Care, Cardiovascular Care, Preventive Screening).']
  supplemental_data_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether supplemental data (e.g., lab results, biometric data) must be collected beyond administrative claims.']
  telehealth_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether services delivered via telehealth can be counted toward measure numerator compliance.']
  type varchar [note: 'Classification of the measure based on what it evaluates (process, outcome, structure, patient experience, efficiency, intermediate outcome, or composite).']
  value_set_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier for the clinical code value sets (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS, LOINC, RxNorm) used in measure specifications.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier for the measure specification, indicating updates or revisions to measure logic.']

  Note: 'Standardized definition of each HEDIS quality measure including numerator, denominator, specifications, and reporting period.'
}

  oversample_count varchar [note: 'Number of additional members included in the sample to account for potential exclusions or missing data.']

  product_line varchar [note: 'Health insurance product line to which the member belongs (Commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Marketplace, Dual Eligible, CHIP).']

  provider_tin varchar [note: 'Tax Identification Number of the provider organization associated with the measure result.']

  rate_percentage decimal(6,2) [note: 'Calculated rate expressed as a percentage (0-100).']
  rate_value decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated rate or percentage for the quality measure (numerator divided by denominator), expressed as a decimal.']
  record_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the measure result record (active, inactive, superseded, deleted).']
  regional_average decimal(10,4) [note: 'Regional average rate for the quality measure for comparison purposes.']
  reportable_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the measure result meets criteria for external reporting (reportable, not reportable, small denominator, data quality issue).']
  reporting_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the measurement period for the quality measure calculation.']
  reporting_period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the measurement period for the quality measure calculation.']
  reporting_year varchar [note: 'The calendar year for which the measure result is calculated and reported.']
  sample_size varchar [note: 'Number of members or records included in the sample for hybrid or survey-based measures.']
  social_determinants_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether social determinants of health factors were considered in the measure calculation or analysis.']

  stratification_category varchar [note: 'Category used for measure stratification (e.g., age group, gender, race/ethnicity, chronic condition).']
  supplemental_data_count varchar [note: 'Number of records with supplemental data (e.g., EHR data, lab results) used in the measure calculation.']
  target_rate decimal(10,4) [note: 'Internal or regulatory target rate established for the quality measure.']
  validated_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the person or system that validated the measure result.']

  zip_code varchar [note: 'ZIP code of the member\'s residence for geographic analysis.']

  Note: 'Calculated result of a HEDIS measure for a member or member group for a specific reporting year.'
}

  Note: 'Master definition of clinical quality metrics (e.g., readmission rate, HbA1c control) with calculation logic.'

Table quality.measure_risk_stratification {
  measure_risk_stratification_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the measure_risk_stratification association']
  hcc_category_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the HCC category used for risk stratification']
  measure_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the quality measure being risk-stratified']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this stratification configuration record was created in the system']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date when this measure-HCC stratification configuration became active for quality calculations']
  end_date date [note: 'The date when this measure-HCC stratification configuration was retired or superseded, null if currently active']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this stratification configuration is currently active for quality measure calculations']
  measure_weight decimal(10,6) [note: 'The weighting factor for this measure-HCC combination used in aggregate quality score calculations']
  risk_adjustment_factor decimal(10,6) [note: 'The numeric adjustment factor applied to this measure when members have this HCC category, used to normalize performance across risk strata']
  stratification_level varchar [note: 'The risk stratification tier assigned to this measure-HCC pairing (e.g., LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, VERY_HIGH) used for reporting and benchmarking']
  updated_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this stratification configuration record was last modified']

  Note: 'This association product represents the risk stratification configuration between quality measures and HCC categories. It captures the risk adjustment methodology used to ensure fair performance comparison across member populations with different health risk profiles. Each record links one quality measure to one HCC category with stratification rules and adjustment factors that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance quality measurement, quality measures (HEDIS, Star Ratings) must be risk-stratified across multiple HCC categories to ensure fair performance comparison between member populations with different health risk profiles. A single quality measure like \'Controlling High Blood Pressure\' applies to multiple HCC categories (diabetes, cardiovascular, renal), and each HCC category is relevant to multiple quality measures. The business actively manages these stratification configurations with specific adjustment factors, weights, and stratification levels for each measure-HCC pairing.'
}

  enrollment_source varchar [note: 'Source or method by which the member was identified and enrolled into this improvement plan (e.g., risk stratification, gap analysis, provider referral).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the enrollment of high-risk members into quality improvement initiatives. Each record links one improvement_plan to one member_risk_profile with attributes that exist only in the context of this enrollment relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, quality improvement plans (such as care gap closure initiatives, chronic disease management programs, and HEDIS measure improvement campaigns) enroll multiple high-risk members simultaneously based on risk stratification and quality measure targeting. Conversely, high-risk members are frequently enrolled in multiple concurrent improvement initiatives addressing different quality domains (e.g., a diabetic member may be enrolled in both a diabetes management plan and a preventive care gap closure plan). Care management teams actively manage these enrollments as operational entities, tracking enrollment dates, completion status, assigned care managers, and target completion dates for each member-plan combination.'
}

Table quality.sanction_remediation {
  sanction_remediation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the sanction_remediation association']
  improvement_plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the quality improvement plan mandated as part of sanction remediation']
  provider_sanction_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the provider sanction requiring remediation']
  assignment_date date [note: 'Date when this improvement plan was formally assigned as a remediation requirement for this sanction.']
  completion_date date [note: 'Date when the provider successfully completed this improvement plan requirement for this sanction.']
  completion_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of remediation requirements completed for this sanction-plan pairing, expressed as 0.00 to 100.00. Identified in detection phase.']
  compliance_deadline date [note: 'The date by which the provider must complete this improvement plan to satisfy sanction remediation requirements. Identified in detection phase.']
  compliance_verification_date date [note: 'Date when compliance with this remediation requirement was formally verified.']
  compliance_verified_by varchar [note: 'Name of the compliance officer or auditor who verified completion of this remediation requirement.']
  monitoring_status varchar [note: 'Current status of compliance monitoring for this specific sanction-plan remediation pairing. Identified in detection phase.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Additional notes or comments regarding this specific sanction-plan remediation relationship.']
  remediation_requirement varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the specific remediation requirement that this improvement plan must address for this sanction. Identified in detection phase.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the remediation relationship between provider sanctions and quality improvement plans. It captures the specific corrective actions, compliance requirements, and monitoring activities mandated for each sanctioned provider. Each record links one provider sanction to one improvement plan with attributes that track remediation progress, compliance deadlines, and completion status.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, provider sanctions for fraud/abuse violations often mandate multiple corrective actions across different domains (clinical quality, billing practices, documentation standards), requiring multiple improvement plans. Conversely, a single improvement plan (e.g., \'Proper Documentation Standards\') can be mandated as remediation for multiple historical sanctions across different providers or violation types. The business actively manages these remediation assignments with specific compliance deadlines, monitoring status, and completion tracking for each sanction-plan pairing.'
}

Each record links one improvement_plan to one agent with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance quality improvement operations, improvement plans require cross-functional teams of service agents with different skills and roles (e.g., training coordinators, data analysts, member outreach specialists) to implement HEDIS and Stars measure improvements. Simultaneously, service agents participate in multiple concurrent improvement initiatives as their skills are needed across different quality domains. The business actively manages these assignments, tracking each agent\'s role, training completion, and contribution hours for accountability and resource planning.'
}

Table quality.provider_measure_performance {
  provider_measure_performance_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the provider_measure_performance association']
  credential_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the credentialed provider being measured']
  measure_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the quality measure being evaluated']
  audit_status varchar [note: 'Status of external audit or validation for this provider-measure performance record']
  benchmark_percentile varchar [note: 'Percentile ranking of this provider\'s performance compared to national or regional benchmarks for this measure']
  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Status indicating whether this provider met the compliance threshold for this measure during this period']
  data_completeness_rate decimal [note: 'Percentage of required data elements available for calculating this provider\'s performance on this measure']
  denominator_count varchar [note: 'Number of this provider\'s eligible patients in the measure denominator during the measurement period']
  exception_count varchar [note: 'Number of patients removed from the denominator for this provider-measure combination due to medical exceptions']
  exclusion_count varchar [note: 'Number of patients excluded from the denominator for this provider-measure combination due to valid clinical or administrative reasons']
  measure_result_value decimal [note: 'Calculated performance rate for this provider on this measure (numerator/denominator), typically expressed as a percentage or ratio']
  measurement_period_end date [note: 'Ending date of the period during which this specific provider\'s performance against this measure was evaluated']
  measurement_period_start date [note: 'Beginning date of the period during which this specific provider\'s performance against this measure was evaluated']
  numerator_count varchar [note: 'Number of this provider\'s patients who met the measure numerator criteria during the measurement period']
  performance_tier varchar [note: 'Categorical rating of provider performance against benchmarks for this measure']
  reporting_year varchar [note: 'Calendar year for which this provider-measure performance is reported to regulatory bodies (NCQA, CMS)']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date when this provider-measure performance result was submitted to regulatory bodies or internal reporting systems']

  Note: 'This association product represents the performance evaluation between quality measures and credentialed providers. It captures provider-specific performance against HEDIS and CMS quality measures for regulatory reporting, Stars ratings, and network performance management. Each record links one quality measure to one credentialed provider with period-specific performance metrics that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, quality measures are evaluated across many credentialed providers, and each provider is measured against multiple quality measures. UnitedHealthcare actively manages provider-specific performance records for HEDIS reporting, CMS Stars ratings, and network performance management, tracking numerator/denominator counts, compliance status, and performance tiers for each provider-measure-period combination.'
}

Table quality.measure_program_target {
  measure_program_target_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the measure_program_target association']
  measure_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the quality measure being tracked']
  program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the program tracking this measure']
  baseline_value decimal(5,2) [note: 'The baseline performance rate for this measure when it was first adopted by this program. Used to calculate improvement over time and ROI for program interventions.']
  budget_allocated decimal(15,2) [note: 'The portion of the program budget allocated specifically to interventions and activities targeting this measure. Enables ROI tracking at the measure-program level.']
  current_value decimal(5,2) [note: 'The most recent calculated performance rate for this measure within this program. Updated based on the reporting frequency.']
  end_date date [note: 'The date when this measure stopped being tracked for this program, if applicable. Measures may be retired from programs due to regulatory changes or program evolution.']
  intervention_strategy varchar [note: 'Description of the specific intervention approach used by this program to improve performance on this measure (e.g., \'Outbound nurse calls for gap closure\', \'Provider incentive program\', \'Member education campaign\').']
  measurement_period varchar [note: 'The specific measurement period for this measure within this program context (e.g., \'2024\', \'2024-2025\'). Programs may track measures on different cycles than the standard HEDIS measurement period.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'The strategic priority assigned to this measure within this specific program (Critical, High, Medium, Low). Priority determines resource allocation, intervention intensity, and reporting frequency. A measure may be High priority in a Diabetes program but Medium in a general wellness program.']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'How often this measure\'s performance is reported within this program context. May differ from the measure\'s standard reporting frequency based on program needs (e.g., monthly for high-priority Star Rating measures in MA programs, quarterly for standard measures).']
  star_rating_weight decimal(3,2) [note: 'The weight or multiplier applied to this measure\'s performance in CMS Star Rating calculations for this program. Only applicable to Medicare Advantage programs. Higher weights indicate greater impact on overall Star Rating.']
  start_date date [note: 'The date when this measure began being tracked for this program. Programs may adopt measures at different times based on regulatory requirements or strategic initiatives.']
  status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this measure-program target (Active, Inactive, Suspended, Under Review). Indicates whether the target is currently being tracked and reported.']
  target_value decimal(5,2) [note: 'The target performance percentage or rate that the program aims to achieve for this specific measure (e.g., 85.00 for 85% compliance). This is program-specific and varies by program type, LOB, and strategic priorities.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational tracking relationship between quality measures and care/quality programs. It captures program-specific performance targets, measurement periods, and reporting requirements for each measure-program combination. Each record links one quality measure to one program with attributes that define how that measure is tracked, reported, and targeted within the specific program context.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, quality measures are tracked across multiple programs (Disease Management, Care Coordination, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid), and each program tracks multiple measures with program-specific targets, priorities, and reporting requirements. For example, the \'Controlling High Blood Pressure\' measure (CBP) may be tracked in a Hypertension Management program with an 85% target and monthly reporting, while also being tracked in a general Medicare Advantage program with a 75% target and quarterly reporting. The business actively manages these measure-program combinations to optimize HEDIS scores, CMS Star Ratings, and quality outcomes.'
}

Table quality.plan_cost_allocation {
  plan_cost_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the plan_cost_allocation association']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the cost center providing budget allocation']
  improvement_plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the quality improvement plan receiving budget allocation']
  actual_spend_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Actual amount spent from this cost center allocation on this improvement plan to date. Tracks utilization of each allocation independently.']
  allocated_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Specific dollar amount allocated from this cost center to this improvement plan. This amount is unique to each cost center-plan combination and represents the cost center\'s financial commitment to the plan.']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of the improvement plan\'s total budget that this cost center is contributing, or percentage of the cost center\'s budget allocated to this plan. This percentage is specific to each allocation relationship.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this specific allocation relationship between the cost center and improvement plan. Tracks the lifecycle of each funding commitment independently.']
  allocation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of how this cost center\'s budget is allocated to this improvement plan (e.g., direct funding, shared services, overhead allocation).']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date when this specific allocation was approved by finance or budget authority.']
  approved_by_name varchar [note: 'Name of the individual who approved this specific cost center allocation to this improvement plan.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was created in the system.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this specific cost center allocation to this improvement plan became effective. Tracks when this funding relationship began.']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when this specific cost center allocation to this improvement plan ends or ended. Supports time-bound funding commitments.']
  last_updated_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that last updated this allocation record.']
  last_updated_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was last modified.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes specific to this allocation relationship, such as special conditions, restrictions, or justifications for this cost center\'s funding of this plan.']
  remaining_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Remaining unspent amount from this specific cost center allocation to this improvement plan.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that created this allocation record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the budget allocation relationship between quality improvement plans and cost centers. It captures how improvement plan budgets are distributed across multiple organizational cost centers, with each allocation tracking the specific amount, percentage, and status of funding from each cost center to each plan. Each record links one improvement plan to one cost center with allocation-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this funding relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance operations, quality improvement plans routinely require budget contributions from multiple cost centers across different departments (clinical operations, IT, care management, analytics). Each cost center tracks its specific allocation amount, percentage, and spending against each plan it funds. Conversely, each cost center typically funds multiple improvement plans simultaneously, creating a genuine many-to-many operational relationship where the allocation itself (with amount, dates, status) is actively managed by finance and quality teams.'
}

  enforcement_level varchar [note: 'The level of enforcement for this specific measure under this compliance policy, indicating whether adherence is required or recommended']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this mandate expires or is scheduled for review (null if ongoing)']
  last_updated_by varchar [note: 'User or system that last updated this mandate relationship record']
  last_updated_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this mandate relationship']
  mandate_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this mandate relationship']
  penalty_amount decimal [note: 'Financial penalty amount (in USD) that may be assessed for failure to meet the required threshold for this measure under this policy']

  required_threshold decimal [note: 'The minimum performance threshold (as a percentage or rate) that must be achieved for this measure to satisfy this specific compliance policy requirement']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or system that created this mandate relationship record']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory mandate relationship between quality measures and compliance policies. It captures the specific requirements, thresholds, and enforcement rules that apply when a compliance policy mandates the tracking and reporting of a quality measure. Each record links one measure to one compliance_policy with attributes that define how that measure must be performed to satisfy that specific policy requirement.. Existence Justification: In health insurance operations, a single quality measure (e.g., Controlling High Blood Pressure) is mandated by multiple compliance policies simultaneously - CMS Star Ratings, state-specific HEDIS requirements, and NCQA accreditation standards each require the same measure with different thresholds, reporting frequencies, and penalties. Conversely, a single compliance policy (e.g., CMS Medicare Advantage regulations) mandates dozens of different quality measures. Compliance teams actively manage these mandate relationships, tracking which measures satisfy which regulatory requirements with specific performance thresholds and enforcement rules.'
}

Each record links one provider score to one audit finding with attributes that exist only in the context of this audit citation relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer audit operations, auditors actively cite provider quality scores as evidence across multiple audit findings (network adequacy, quality of care, credentialing, Stars rating compliance). A single provider score can be referenced in multiple findings across different audits or within the same audit, and a single audit finding typically documents multiple provider scores as supporting evidence. Auditors create citation records that capture the score value at audit time, assign severity, track remediation deadlines, and manage validation status.'

Table quality.measure_requirement {

  reporting_deadline_offset_days varchar [note: 'Number of days after measurement period end by which this measure must be reported for this benefit design to regulatory bodies']

  status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this measure requirement for this benefit design']
  termination_date date [note: 'Date when this measure requirement is no longer applicable for this benefit design due to regulatory changes or plan termination']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory requirement between quality measures and government benefit designs. It captures the mandatory reporting obligations, compliance thresholds, and measurement specifications that apply when a specific HEDIS or CMS quality measure is required for a particular government program benefit design. Each record links one measure to one benefit design with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory requirement.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, government programs (Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Dual Eligible SNPs) each mandate different sets of HEDIS and CMS quality measures with program-specific reporting requirements, compliance thresholds, and measurement frequencies. A single quality measure like \'Controlling High Blood Pressure\' applies to multiple benefit designs (MA PPO, MA HMO, Medicaid Managed Care) with different thresholds and reporting frequencies, while each benefit design must comply with multiple quality measures simultaneously. The business actively manages these regulatory requirements as a compliance function.'
}

  subscriber_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the primary subscriber on the policy associated with the rule violation.']
  subscriber_member_profile_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the primary subscriber on the policy associated with the rule violation.']
  transaction_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the originating transaction (claim, payment, enrollment) that violated the fraud detection rule.']
  type_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fraud.fraud_type. Business justification: Rule_violation should reference fraud_type for standardized fraud classification. Currently uses rule_category string which should be replaced with fraud_type_id FK.']
  actual_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Actual value from the transaction that was compared against the rule threshold.']
  allowed_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount allowed by the health plan for the service according to contract terms.']
  audit_type varchar [note: 'Type of provider audit associated with the rule violation (e.g., prepayment, postpayment).']
  authorization_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether prior authorization was required for the service that violated the rule.']
  billed_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total amount billed by the provider for the service that violated the rule.']

  pharmacy_ndc varchar [note: 'National Drug Code for pharmacy claims that violated the rule.']

  place_of_service_code varchar [note: 'Two-digit code identifying where the service was rendered.']
  prior_authorization_number varchar [note: 'Prior authorization number associated with the service, if the violation relates to authorization bypass.']
  procedure_code varchar [note: 'CPT, HCPCS, or ICD procedure code associated with the service that violated the rule.']
  procedure_code_type varchar [note: 'Type of procedure code used (CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10-PCS, Revenue Code).']
  provider_name varchar [note: 'Name of the healthcare provider associated with the transaction that violated the rule.']
  provider_npi varchar [note: 'National Provider Identifier of the provider associated with the transaction that violated the rule.']
  provider_specialty varchar [note: 'Medical specialty of the provider associated with the rule violation.']
  provider_tin varchar [note: 'Tax Identification Number of the provider associated with the rule violation.']
  provider_type varchar [note: 'Type of healthcare provider involved in the rule violation.']
  recovery_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount recovered from the provider or member as a result of the rule violation investigation.']
  recovery_date date [note: 'Date when the overpayment was recovered from the provider or member.']
  recovery_method varchar [note: 'Method used to recover the overpayment (e.g., offset, refund, installment plan).']
  referral_agency varchar [note: 'Name of the law enforcement or regulatory agency to which the violation was referred.']
  referral_date date [note: 'Date when the rule violation was referred to external agencies.']
  referral_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rule violation was referred to law enforcement or regulatory agencies.']
  resolution_code varchar [note: 'Code indicating the outcome of the rule violation investigation.']
  resolution_notes varchar [note: 'Detailed notes documenting the resolution of the rule violation investigation.']
  resolution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the rule violation investigation was resolved or closed.']
  revenue_code varchar [note: 'Revenue code from the institutional claim that violated the rule.']
  review_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the rule violation was reviewed by an investigator.']
  risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Risk score assigned to the violation based on severity, amount, and historical patterns.']
  rule_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive name of the fraud detection rule that was violated.']
  service_date date [note: 'Date of service for the healthcare transaction that violated the rule.']
  service_from_date date [note: 'Start date of the service period for the transaction that violated the rule.']
  service_to_date date [note: 'End date of the service period for the transaction that violated the rule.']
  threshold_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Threshold value defined in the rule that was exceeded or violated.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Type of transaction that triggered the rule violation (e.g., claim, payment, enrollment, prior authorization).']
  units_of_service varchar [note: 'Number of units of service billed that may have triggered the rule violation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the rule violation record was last updated.']
  validated_fraud_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rule violation was confirmed as actual fraud after investigation.']
  variance_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Difference between the actual value and the threshold value, indicating the magnitude of the violation.']
  variance_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage variance between actual value and threshold value.']
  violation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Monetary amount associated with the rule violation, representing potential overpayment or fraudulent charge.']
  violation_date date [note: 'Date when the rule violation was detected, used for daily reporting and aggregation.']
  violation_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the rule violation including specific conditions that were breached.']
  violation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the rule violation in the investigation workflow.']
  violation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the rule violation was detected by the fraud detection system.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of each rule violation that triggered a fraud alert, linking to the originating transaction.'
}

  type_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fraud.fraud_type. Business justification: Recovery_action should reference fraud_type for standardized fraud classification. Currently uses fraud_category string which should be replaced with fraud_type_id FK.']
  action_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code indicating the reason for the recovery action such as overpayment, duplicate payment, fraud, or billing error.']
  action_reason_description varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of why the recovery action was initiated including specific findings from the investigation or audit.']
  action_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the recovery action in its lifecycle from initiation to closure.']
  action_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the recovery method being pursued to reclaim overpaid or improperly paid funds.']
  administrative_fee decimal(15,2) [note: 'Administrative processing fee charged to cover the cost of recovery operations and investigation.']
  appeal_date date [note: 'Date when the provider filed a formal appeal or dispute of the recovery action.']
  appeal_decision_date date [note: 'Date when a final decision was rendered on the provider appeal or dispute.']

  claims_with_errors_count varchar [note: 'Number of claims identified with billing errors, overpayments, or fraudulent activity during the audit or investigation.']

  cms_reported_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the overpayment and recovery action have been reported to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) as required for Medicare and Medicaid programs.']
  collection_agency_name varchar [note: 'Name of the external third-party collection agency handling the recovery action.']
  collection_agency_referral_date date [note: 'Date when the recovery action was referred to the external collection agency.']
  collection_method varchar [note: 'Method by which the recovery amount is being collected from the provider or responsible party.']
  contract_termination_date date [note: 'Date when the provider contract was terminated as a result of the fraud, waste, or abuse findings.']
  contract_termination_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the provider contract has been terminated as a result of the fraud, waste, or abuse findings.']
  court_case_number varchar [note: 'Official case number assigned by the court if the recovery action has resulted in litigation.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO currency code for all monetary amounts in this recovery action.']

  exclusion_date date [note: 'Date when the provider was excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs.']
  exclusion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the provider has been excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs as a result of the fraud findings.']
  external_collection_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the recovery action has been referred to an external third-party collection agency.']
  first_collection_date date [note: 'Date when the first payment or recovery amount was collected from the provider.']
  initiated_date date [note: 'Date when the recovery action was formally initiated following investigation findings.']
  installment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Dollar amount of each installment payment if the provider is on an installment plan.']
  installment_count varchar [note: 'Total number of installment payments agreed upon if the provider is on an installment plan.']
  installment_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which installment payments are due if the provider is on an installment plan.']
  installment_plan_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the provider has been granted an installment payment plan to repay the recovery amount over time.']
  interest_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Additional interest charges applied to the overpayment amount per contractual or regulatory requirements.']
  judgment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Dollar amount awarded by the court in a legal judgment related to this recovery action.']
  judgment_date date [note: 'Date when the court issued a legal judgment related to this recovery action.']
  last_collection_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent payment or recovery amount collected from the provider.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this recovery action record was last updated in the source system.']
  law_enforcement_agency varchar [note: 'Name of the law enforcement agency to which the case was referred such as FBI, state attorney general, or local fraud unit.']
  law_enforcement_referral_date date [note: 'Date when the case was formally referred to law enforcement for criminal investigation.']
  law_enforcement_referral_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the case has been referred to law enforcement agencies for criminal investigation.']

  offset_applied_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the recovery amount has been or will be offset against future claim payments to the provider.']

  payment_due_date date [note: 'Date by which the provider is required to remit payment or the recovery amount will be subject to offset or further action.']

  provider_tin varchar [note: 'Federal Tax Identification Number of the provider subject to recovery action.']
  provider_type varchar [note: 'Type of healthcare provider from whom funds are being recovered such as physician, hospital, pharmacy, or Durable Medical Equipment (DME) supplier.']
  recovery_amount_collected decimal(15,2) [note: 'Actual dollar amount successfully recovered to date through this recovery action.']

  settlement_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Agreed-upon dollar amount in a settlement agreement which may differ from the original recovery amount requested.']
  settlement_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether the recovery action was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement with the provider.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the operational system from which this recovery action record originated such as payment integrity platform or Special Investigations Unit (SIU) case management system.']

  state_report_date date [note: 'Date when the fraud case and recovery action were reported to the state insurance department or fraud bureau.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of actions taken to recover funds, such as recoupment, offset, or legal action.'
}

Table fraud.type {
  type_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the fraud type classification. Primary key for the fraud type reference table.']
  average_financial_impact decimal(15,2) [note: 'Average dollar amount of financial loss per occurrence of this fraud type, used for risk prioritization and resource allocation.']
  average_investigation_days varchar [note: 'Typical number of days required to complete investigation of this fraud type, used for case planning and resource allocation.']
  category varchar [note: 'High-level category classifying the fraud type by perpetrator or area (provider fraud, member fraud, pharmacy fraud, billing fraud, medical necessity fraud, identity fraud, network fraud).']
  claim_type_applicability varchar [note: 'Types of claims where this fraud type is typically observed (e.g., professional claims, institutional claims, pharmacy claims, dental claims).']
  cms_program_integrity_category varchar [note: 'CMS program integrity category classification for Medicare and Medicaid fraud types, used for federal reporting and coordination.']
  code varchar [note: 'Short alphanumeric code representing the fraud type for system processing and reporting (e.g., DUP_BILL, UPCODE, PHANTOM_PROV).']
  conviction_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Historical percentage of investigated cases of this fraud type that resulted in criminal conviction or civil settlement, indicating prosecutability.']
  created_date date [note: 'Date when this fraud type record was originally created in the reference table.']
  data_sources varchar [note: 'Key data sources and systems used to detect and investigate this fraud type (e.g., claims data, provider enrollment, pharmacy data, external databases).']
  description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the fraud type including characteristics, patterns, and typical indicators used by Special Investigations Unit (SIU) teams.']
  detection_method varchar [note: 'Primary method typically used to detect this fraud type (automated rules, predictive analytics, manual review, provider audit, member complaint, whistleblower, data mining, peer comparison).']
  education_materials_available boolean [note: 'Indicates whether provider or member education materials are available to prevent this fraud type through awareness and compliance training.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this fraud type classification became effective and available for use in fraud detection and case management systems.']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when this fraud type classification was retired or superseded, null if currently active.']
  fwa_classification varchar [note: 'Classification indicating whether this type represents fraud (intentional deception), waste (overutilization without intent), or abuse (practices inconsistent with standards).']
  historical_prevalence_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Historical rate of occurrence for this fraud type as a percentage of total claims or providers, used for risk modeling and resource planning.']
  investigation_priority varchar [note: 'Standard priority level assigned to investigations of this fraud type by the Special Investigations Unit (SIU).']
  involves_organized_crime boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this fraud type is commonly associated with organized crime rings or sophisticated fraud schemes requiring specialized investigation.']
  last_updated_date date [note: 'Date when this fraud type record was last modified or reviewed.']
  lob_applicability varchar [note: 'Lines of business where this fraud type is commonly encountered (e.g., Commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Individual Exchange).']
  mandatory_reporting_threshold decimal(15,2) [note: 'Dollar threshold above which cases of this fraud type must be reported to external authorities per regulatory requirements.']
  naic_fraud_code varchar [note: 'NAIC standardized fraud classification code for industry-wide reporting and benchmarking.']
  name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the fraud type (e.g., Duplicate Billing, Upcoding, Phantom Provider).']
  peer_comparison_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether peer comparison analytics (comparing provider patterns to specialty peers) is effective for detecting this fraud type.']
  postpayment_audit_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether postpayment provider audits are an effective method for detecting this fraud type after claims have been paid.']
  prepayment_edit_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether prepayment claim edits can effectively prevent or detect this fraud type before payment is issued.']
  prevention_strategy varchar [note: 'Recommended prevention strategies and controls to reduce occurrence of this fraud type (e.g., prepayment edits, provider education, enhanced credentialing).']
  provider_specialty_risk varchar [note: 'Provider specialties or types that are at higher risk for this fraud type (e.g., DME suppliers, home health agencies, pain management clinics).']
  recovery_method varchar [note: 'Primary method used to recover overpayments for this fraud type (offset against future payments, demand letter, payment plan, legal action, write-off).']
  regulatory_citation varchar [note: 'Specific laws, regulations, or statutes that define or prohibit this fraud type (e.g., False Claims Act 31 USC 3729, Anti-Kickback Statute 42 USC 1320a-7b).']
  requires_clinical_review boolean [note: 'Indicates whether investigation of this fraud type requires clinical expertise or medical director review to assess medical necessity or appropriateness.']
  requires_external_data boolean [note: 'Indicates whether investigation of this fraud type typically requires data from external sources (e.g., law enforcement databases, other payers, public records).']
  requires_law_enforcement_referral boolean [note: 'Indicates whether confirmed cases of this fraud type typically require referral to law enforcement agencies or regulatory bodies.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Severity classification indicating the typical financial impact and urgency of investigation for this fraud type.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the source system or authority that defined this fraud type classification (e.g., Cotiviti Payment Accuracy, Internal SIU, NAIC, CMS).']
  status varchar [note: 'Current status of this fraud type classification in the reference table (active for current use, inactive if no longer applicable, under review if being evaluated, deprecated if replaced).']
  statute_of_limitations_years varchar [note: 'Number of years within which legal action can be taken for this fraud type, based on applicable federal and state laws.']
  subcategory varchar [note: 'Secondary classification providing additional granularity within the fraud category (e.g., within provider fraud: billing schemes, kickback schemes, credential abuse).']
  typical_indicators varchar [note: 'Common red flags and patterns that indicate potential occurrence of this fraud type, used by investigators and automated detection systems.']
  version varchar [note: 'Version number of this fraud type definition, incremented when classification criteria or attributes are updated.']

  Note: 'Reference table enumerating standardized fraud types (e.g., duplicate billing, upcoding, phantom providers).'
}

Individual HCC assignments can be audited multiple times through different audit types (annual compliance audits, targeted reviews, CMS RADV audits). The business actively manages audit findings as operational records with specific validation statuses, documentation quality scores, error types, and financial impacts for each HCC assignment reviewed.'

Table fraud.policy_violation {
  policy_violation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the policy_violation association']

  policy_section_violated varchar [note: 'Specific section, clause, or provision of the compliance policy that was violated (corresponds to policy_section_violated from detection data)']
  remediation_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether remediation action is required for this specific policy violation']

  reported_to_regulator_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator of whether this policy violation was reported to external regulatory authorities']

  violation_severity varchar [note: 'Severity classification of this specific policy violation as determined by the investigation (corresponds to violation_severity from detection data)']

  Note: 'This association product represents the violation event between investigation and compliance_policy. It captures the specific instance where a fraud investigation identifies a violation of a particular compliance policy. Each record links one investigation to one compliance_policy with attributes that document the violation details, severity, and findings for regulatory reporting and remediation tracking.. Existence Justification: In health insurance fraud investigations, a single investigation routinely identifies violations of multiple compliance policies (HIPAA privacy rules, Anti-Kickback Statute, False Claims Act, billing policies, etc.), and each compliance policy can be violated across many different investigations. The business actively manages policy violations as distinct operational records with specific findings, severity assessments, and regulatory reporting requirements for each investigation-policy combination.'
}

Table fraud.investigation_program_scope {
  investigation_program_scope_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the investigation_program_scope association']
  investigation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fraud investigation case']
  provider_program_participation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the provider program participation record under investigation']
  assigned_investigator varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the investigator assigned to investigate this specific program participation (from detection phase: assigned_investigator)']
  closed_date date [note: 'Date when investigation of this specific program participation was closed']
  confirmed_program_loss_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Confirmed financial loss specific to this program participation']
  estimated_program_loss_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Estimated financial loss specific to this program participation']
  findings_summary varchar [note: 'Summary of investigation findings specific to this program participation']
  program_specific_violations varchar [note: 'Documented violations specific to this program participation such as billing irregularities, quality issues, or compliance failures (from detection phase: program_specific_violations)']
  scope varchar [note: 'Detailed scope of investigation for this specific program participation including claims periods, service types, and geographic areas under review (from detection phase: investigation_scope)']
  start_date date [note: 'Date when investigation of this specific program participation began (from detection phase: investigation_start_date)']
  status varchar [note: 'Current status of the investigation for this specific program participation (from detection phase: investigation_status)']

  Note: 'This association product represents the investigative scope between fraud investigations and provider program participations. It captures the specific government programs under investigation, program-specific violations discovered, investigation status per program, and assigned investigators. Each record links one investigation to one provider program participation with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer fraud operations, a single investigation routinely examines multiple government program participations when providers commit cross-program fraud (e.g., billing fraud across Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and CHIP simultaneously). Conversely, a single provider program participation can be subject to multiple concurrent or sequential investigations for different fraud types (billing irregularities, kickback schemes, quality violations). SIU investigators actively manage investigation scope records per program, tracking program-specific violations, findings, status, and assigned investigators.'
}

  remediation_completed_date date [note: 'The date when remediation or corrective action was completed and verified for this investigation.']
  remediation_due_date date [note: 'The date by which remediation or corrective action must be completed for audit findings related to this investigation.']
  remediation_required boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether remediation or corrective action is required for this investigation based on audit findings.']
  review_status varchar [note: 'The current status of the audit review for this specific investigation. Tracks the progression from initial selection for audit through completion of review and resolution of findings.']
  sample_selection_reason varchar [note: 'The reason why this investigation was selected for inclusion in the audit sample (e.g., \'High dollar amount\', \'Random statistical sample\', \'Risk-based selection\', \'Prior audit finding follow-up\').']
  scope varchar [note: 'The specific scope of the audit as it pertains to this particular investigation. Describes what aspects of the investigation were reviewed (e.g., \'Evidence collection procedures\', \'Financial calculations\', \'Compliance with SIU protocols\'). This is investigation-specific and differs from the overall audit scope.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the audit event between investigation and audit. It captures the formal review and examination of fraud investigation cases by internal compliance teams, external auditors, or regulatory bodies. Each record links one investigation to one audit engagement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific audit review, including the scope of review, findings specific to that investigation, and the auditor assigned to review that particular case.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, fraud investigations are subject to multiple types of audits throughout their lifecycle: internal quality assurance reviews, compliance audits, regulatory audits (CMS, state insurance departments), and legal sufficiency reviews. Conversely, a single audit engagement (e.g., annual SIU compliance audit) examines a sample of multiple investigation cases to assess overall program effectiveness, adherence to protocols, and regulatory compliance. The business actively manages this relationship by tracking which investigations were audited, what findings were identified per investigation, and what remediation is required.'
}

Table risk.factor {
  factor_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the risk factor record. Primary key for the risk factor reference table.']
  model_version_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to risk.model_version. Business justification: risk_factor stores model_version as STRING. Adding FK to model_version reference table establishes authoritative link to the CMS model version for which this risk factor applies. No columns to remove ']
  aca_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to ACA marketplace risk adjustment. ACA uses HHS-HCC model which differs from CMS-HCC model for Medicare Advantage.']
  adult_model_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to the adult risk adjustment model (age 21+). CMS uses separate models for adults, children, and infants.']
  age_range varchar [note: 'Age range bracket for demographic factors. CMS uses specific age bands for risk adjustment. Null for non-demographic factors.']
  average_incremental_cost decimal(12,2) [note: 'Average incremental annual cost (in dollars) associated with this factor, based on CMS regression analysis. Represents the additional expected cost beyond the baseline for a beneficiary with this factor.']
  benchmark_county_rate decimal(10,2) [note: 'Average county-level benchmark rate (in dollars) used with this factor for payment calculations. CMS sets county-specific benchmarks that are multiplied by RAF scores to determine plan payments.']
  care_management_program_eligibility varchar [note: 'Care management or disease management programs for which members with this HCC are typically eligible (e.g., \'Diabetes Management\', \'Heart Failure Program\', \'Complex Case Management\').']
  child_model_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to the child risk adjustment model (age 2-20). Child models have different factors reflecting pediatric conditions.']
  chronic_condition_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this HCC represents a chronic condition that typically persists across multiple years. Chronic conditions are expected to recur annually in diagnosis data.']
  clinical_category varchar [note: 'High-level clinical category grouping for HCC factors (e.g., cardiovascular, diabetes, respiratory). Facilitates clinical analysis and reporting. Null for demographic factors.']
  cms_publication_date date [note: 'Date when CMS officially published this factor in the rate notice or model documentation. Establishes regulatory effective date.']
  coding_intensity_adjustment decimal(6,4) [note: 'Adjustment factor applied by CMS to account for year-over-year increases in diagnosis coding intensity that do not reflect true changes in beneficiary health status. Typically a value less than 1.0 that reduces RAF scores.']
  coefficient_value decimal(10,6) [note: 'The numeric coefficient value used in RAF score calculation. This value is multiplied by the presence indicator (0 or 1) and summed across all applicable factors to produce the member\'s total RAF score. Higher values indicate greater expected cost.']
  demographic_category varchar [note: 'Demographic classification for this factor: age_gender for standard age/sex combinations, medicaid for dual eligible status, disability for disabled beneficiaries, institutional for nursing home residents, ltimcaid for long-term institutional Medicaid, origds for originally disabled, new_enrollee for first-year enrollees. Null for pure HCC factors.']
  disease_hierarchy_child varchar [note: 'Child HCC in the disease hierarchy. Represents the more severe condition that suppresses the parent HCC.']
  disease_hierarchy_parent varchar [note: 'Parent HCC in the disease hierarchy. When a more severe condition (child) is present, less severe conditions (parent) are suppressed and their factors are not counted. Implements the hierarchical nature of HCC model.']
  documentation_requirements varchar [note: 'Summary of clinical documentation requirements for this HCC to be considered valid in RADV audits. Describes what must be present in the medical record to support the diagnosis.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this risk factor becomes effective for use in RAF calculations. Typically January 1 of the payment year.']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when this risk factor is no longer effective. Null for currently active factors. Factors may be retired or replaced in new model versions.']
  esrd_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to beneficiaries with End Stage Renal Disease. ESRD beneficiaries use a separate risk adjustment model with different factors.']
  final_rule_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor has been finalized in a CMS final rule and is ready for operational use. False for proposed factors still under review.']
  gender varchar [note: 'Gender classification for demographic factors (male or female). Null for non-demographic factors or gender-neutral factors.']
  hcc_code varchar [note: 'The HCC code to which this factor applies (e.g., HCC18, HCC85). Null for pure demographic factors. HCCs represent clinically and cost-related groupings of diagnoses.']
  hcc_label varchar [note: 'Descriptive label for the HCC code (e.g., \'Diabetes with Chronic Complications\', \'Congestive Heart Failure\'). Provides clinical context for the condition category.']
  hedis_measure_linkage varchar [note: 'HEDIS quality measures associated with this HCC (e.g., \'CDC-Diabetes Care\', \'CBP-Controlling High Blood Pressure\'). Links risk adjustment to quality reporting requirements.']
  hhs_hcc_code varchar [note: 'The HHS-HCC code for ACA marketplace risk adjustment. HHS-HCC categories differ from CMS-HCC categories. Null for Medicare factors.']
  icd10_mapping_count varchar [note: 'Number of ICD-10 diagnosis codes that map to this HCC. Provides indication of the breadth of diagnoses included in the condition category. Null for demographic factors.']
  infant_model_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to the infant risk adjustment model (age 0-1). Infant models include factors for birth complications and congenital conditions.']
  inpatient_cost_impact varchar [note: 'Relative impact of this condition on inpatient hospitalization costs: high for conditions with frequent or expensive hospitalizations, medium for moderate inpatient utilization, low for minimal inpatient impact, none for no inpatient component.']
  institutional_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to community-dwelling or institutionalized (nursing home) beneficiaries. CMS uses separate models for these populations.']
  interaction_component_1 varchar [note: 'First component of an interaction factor (e.g., HCC code or demographic category). Interaction factors apply when multiple conditions or characteristics co-occur, capturing additional risk beyond additive effects.']
  interaction_component_2 varchar [note: 'Second component of an interaction factor. Null for non-interaction factors.']
  interaction_component_3 varchar [note: 'Third component of an interaction factor for three-way interactions. Null for two-way interactions or non-interaction factors.']
  last_updated_date date [note: 'Date when this risk factor record was last updated in the reference table. Used for change tracking and data quality validation.']
  ma_only_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies only to Medicare Advantage plans and not to other CMS programs (e.g., ACA marketplace risk adjustment uses different factors).']
  maturity_adjustment decimal(6,4) [note: 'Adjustment factor for new or low-enrollment plans to account for incomplete diagnosis capture. Applied as a multiplier to RAF scores for plans below maturity thresholds.']
  medicaid_status varchar [note: 'Medicaid dual eligibility status for demographic factors: full_benefit for full dual eligibles, partial_benefit for partial dual eligibles, non_dual for Medicare-only. Null if not applicable to this factor.']
  model_segment varchar [note: 'CMS model segment to which this factor applies: CNA (Community Non-dual Aged), CND (Community Non-dual Disabled), CFA (Community Full-benefit dual Aged), CFD (Community Full-benefit dual Disabled), CPA (Community Partial-benefit dual Aged), CPD (Community Partial-benefit dual Disabled), INS (Institutional), NE (New Enrollee), SNPNE (SNP New Enrollee). Each segment has distinct factor values.']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version of the CMS risk adjustment model to which this factor applies (e.g., V24, V28). Each model year may have different factor values.']
  normalization_factor decimal(10,6) [note: 'Normalization factor applied to ensure the average RAF score across the population equals 1.0. CMS adjusts factors annually to maintain budget neutrality.']
  originally_disabled_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to beneficiaries who originally qualified for Medicare through disability (ORIGDS). Originally disabled beneficiaries have different risk profiles even after aging into Medicare.']
  outpatient_cost_impact varchar [note: 'Relative impact of this condition on outpatient and professional services costs: high for conditions requiring frequent specialist visits or procedures, medium for moderate outpatient utilization, low for minimal outpatient impact, none for no outpatient component.']
  part_c_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to Medicare Part C (Medical) risk adjustment.']
  part_d_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor applies to Medicare Part D (Prescription Drug) risk adjustment. Part D uses a separate RxHCC model with different factors.']
  payment_year varchar [note: 'Calendar year for which this risk factor applies for payment calculations. Risk factors are updated annually by CMS.']
  pharmacy_cost_impact varchar [note: 'Relative impact of this condition on pharmacy costs: high for conditions requiring expensive medications, medium for moderate pharmacy utilization, low for minimal pharmacy impact, none for no pharmacy component.']
  prevalence_rate decimal(6,4) [note: 'Proportion of the Medicare Advantage population with this factor present, based on CMS national data. Used for benchmarking and validation. Value between 0 and 1.']
  prior_authorization_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether services related to this condition typically require prior authorization. Used to link risk adjustment to utilization management processes.']
  public_comment_period_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this factor is currently in public comment period (proposed but not finalized). CMS releases draft rate notices for public comment before finalizing.']
  radv_audit_frequency varchar [note: 'Relative frequency with which this HCC is selected for RADV audits by CMS: high for frequently audited HCCs (high-value, high-risk), medium for moderately audited, low for rarely audited. Null for demographic factors.']
  recapture_eligible_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this HCC is eligible for recapture in chart review programs. Some HCCs are prioritized for retrospective documentation and coding review to ensure complete risk capture.']
  rxhcc_code varchar [note: 'The RxHCC code for Part D risk adjustment factors. RxHCCs are similar to HCCs but specific to pharmacy risk. Null for Part C factors.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Relative severity classification of the condition represented by this HCC: low, moderate, high, or very_high. Based on coefficient value and clinical judgment. Null for demographic factors.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'System from which this factor definition was loaded: RAPS (Risk Adjustment Processing System) for legacy Medicare Advantage, EDPS (Encounter Data Processing System) for current MA, ACA_EDGE for marketplace, manual for manually maintained reference data.']
  star_rating_impact varchar [note: 'Relative impact of this condition on CMS Star Ratings quality measures: high for conditions directly measured in Star Ratings (e.g., diabetes control), medium for indirect impact, low for minimal impact, none for no impact.']
  status varchar [note: 'Current status of the risk factor: active for factors in current use, inactive for retired factors, superseded for factors replaced by newer versions, proposed for factors in draft rate notices not yet finalized.']
  suspect_condition_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this HCC is flagged as a suspect condition requiring additional documentation or validation. Used in chart review and coding compliance programs.']
  type varchar [note: 'Type of risk factor: HCC (Hierarchical Condition Category) for disease-based factors, demographic for age/gender factors, interaction for combined demographic and disease factors, or disease_interaction for multiple HCC combinations.']
  version_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes describing changes to this factor in the current model version compared to prior versions. Documents CMS rationale for coefficient changes, new factors, or retired factors.']

  Note: 'Reference table of factor values applied to HCCs and demographic attributes for RAF calculation.'
}

  error_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of any processing error encountered during reconciliation.']
  financial_impact_category varchar [note: 'Classification of the financial significance of the reconciliation adjustment.']
  hcc_codes_added varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of HCC codes added during reconciliation that were not in the original risk score calculation.']
  hcc_codes_removed varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of HCC codes removed during reconciliation that were in the original risk score calculation.']
  hcc_count_adjusted varchar [note: 'Number of HCC codes included in the adjusted RAF score calculation after reconciliation.']
  hcc_count_original varchar [note: 'Number of HCC codes included in the original RAF score calculation.']
  institutional_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the member resides in an institutional setting, affecting risk adjustment.']
  interaction_factor_adjusted decimal(10,6) [note: 'Interaction component of the adjusted RAF score after reconciliation.']
  interaction_factor_original decimal(10,6) [note: 'Interaction component of the original RAF score based on disease-disease or disease-demographic interactions.']
  line_of_business varchar [note: 'Product line or line of business for the member\'s plan.']
  medicaid_dual_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the member\'s Medicaid dual eligibility status affecting risk adjustment.']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version of the CMS HCC risk adjustment model used for the reconciliation calculation.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments regarding the reconciliation adjustment.']
  original_payment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Initial CMS payment amount calculated based on the original RAF score.']
  original_raf_score decimal(10,6) [note: 'Initial RAF score calculated for the member before reconciliation adjustments.']
  part_d_enrollment_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the member is enrolled in Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage.']
  payment_adjustment_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the reconciliation resulted in a payment increase, decrease, or no change.']
  payment_variance_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Dollar difference between original and adjusted payment amounts (adjusted minus original).']
  payment_year varchar [note: 'Calendar year for which CMS risk-adjusted payments are being reconciled.']
  processing_priority varchar [note: 'Priority level assigned to the reconciliation for processing queue management.']
  provider_npi varchar [note: 'Ten-digit NPI of the provider who documented the diagnosis codes involved in the reconciliation.']
  provider_specialty_code varchar [note: 'CMS specialty code for the provider who documented the diagnosis.']
  raf_score_variance decimal(10,6) [note: 'Difference between the original and adjusted RAF scores (adjusted minus original).']
  reason_code varchar [note: 'Code indicating the specific reason for the risk score adjustment or reconciliation.']
  reason_description varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of why the risk score reconciliation was necessary.']
  region_code varchar [note: 'Geographic region code where the member is enrolled.']
  reprocessing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this reconciliation record is a reprocessed version of a previous submission.']
  reversal_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this reconciliation record reverses a previous adjustment.']
  reversed_reconciliation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the reconciliation record being reversed by this transaction.']
  risk_score_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the risk score in the CMS reconciliation lifecycle.']
  run_date date [note: 'Date when the reconciliation batch process was executed.']
  service_from_date date [note: 'Start date of the service period for the encounter or claim that triggered the reconciliation.']
  service_through_date date [note: 'End date of the service period for the encounter or claim that triggered the reconciliation.']
  source_record_id varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the record in the source system that triggered the reconciliation.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the source system that generated the reconciliation data.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date when the RAPS or EDPS data was submitted to CMS.']
  type varchar [note: 'Classification of the reconciliation event indicating the stage in the CMS payment cycle.']
  validation_error_count varchar [note: 'Number of validation errors identified during reconciliation processing.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the reconciliation passed internal validation checks.']

  Note: 'Transactional log of adjustments made to reconcile calculated risk scores with CMS payment outcomes.'
}

Adding FK to model_version reference table establishes authoritative link to the CMS model version for which this rule applies. No columns to remove as model_']

  audit_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rule is subject to special audit scrutiny or validation requirements due to high payment impact or fraud risk.']
  change_reason varchar [note: 'Description of the reason for the most recent change to this rule, including regulatory updates, model recalibration, or error corrections.']

  gap_closure_priority varchar [note: 'Priority level for targeting members with suspected but undocumented conditions covered by this rule in gap closure outreach programs.']
  gender varchar [note: 'The gender to which this risk adjustment rule applies. Some demographic factors are gender-specific.']
  hcc_code varchar [note: 'The specific HCC code that this rule applies to or generates. HCCs are condition categories used in CMS risk adjustment models to predict healthcare costs.']
