  audit_trail_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a detailed audit trail must be maintained for all allocation transactions generated by this rule.']
  auto_post_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocation transactions generated by this rule are automatically posted to the general ledger without manual intervention.']
  business_unit varchar [note: 'The business unit or division to which this allocation rule applies.']
  calculation_precision varchar [note: 'The number of decimal places to which allocation calculations are rounded.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this allocation rule was created in the system.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which allocation amounts are denominated.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'The date on which this allocation rule ceases to be active and is no longer applied to financial transactions.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date from which this allocation rule becomes active and begins to be applied to financial transactions.']
  expense_category varchar [note: 'The high-level expense category classification for the allocated amount.']
  functional_area varchar [note: 'The functional area or department to which costs are allocated (e.g., claims operations, member services, provider relations, underwriting).']
  gaap_reporting_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocations generated by this rule are included in GAAP-basis financial reporting.']
  geography_code varchar [note: 'The geographic region or state code to which this allocation rule applies (ISO 3166 country codes or US state codes).']
  is_intercompany boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this allocation rule involves intercompany transactions between legal entities requiring elimination entries.']
  is_reciprocal boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this allocation rule participates in reciprocal allocation where costs are allocated back and forth between cost centers.']
  legal_entity varchar [note: 'The legal entity identifier to which this allocation rule applies for statutory and regulatory reporting purposes.']
  lob varchar [note: 'The health insurance line of business to which this allocation rule applies (commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, dual eligible, individual, group, ASO, fully insured, government programs, or specialty).']
  maximum_allocation_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The maximum dollar amount cap that can be allocated under this rule in a single allocation cycle.']
  minimum_allocation_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The minimum dollar amount threshold below which the allocation rule will not be applied.']
  mlr_category varchar [note: 'The MLR category classification for allocated costs used in ACA medical loss ratio calculations (medical claims, quality improvement, fraud prevention, administrative, excluded, or non-claims cost).']
  modified_by varchar [note: 'The user identifier or name of the person who last modified this allocation rule.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this allocation rule was last modified in the system.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-form text field for additional notes, comments, or documentation about the allocation rule.']
  plan_type varchar [note: 'The type of health plan to which this allocation rule applies (HMO, PPO, EPO, POS, HDHP, indemnity, Medicare Advantage, PDP, SNP, or Medicaid managed care).']
  priority_order varchar [note: 'The sequence order in which this allocation rule is executed when multiple rules apply. Lower numbers execute first.']
  regulatory_reporting_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocations generated by this rule are used in regulatory reporting submissions to CMS, state insurance departments, or other regulatory bodies.']
  requires_approval boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocation transactions generated by this rule require management approval before posting to the general ledger.']
  retired_by varchar [note: 'The user identifier or name of the person who retired or deactivated this allocation rule.']
  retired_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this allocation rule was retired or deactivated.']
  reversal_allowed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocation transactions generated by this rule can be reversed or adjusted after posting.']
  rounding_method varchar [note: 'The method used to round allocation amounts (round up, round down, round to nearest, or truncate).']
  rule_code varchar [note: 'Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the allocation rule for business reference and reporting purposes.']
  rule_description varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of the allocation rule purpose, methodology, and business rationale.']
  rule_formula varchar [note: 'The mathematical formula or expression used to calculate the allocation amount. May reference allocation basis metrics and weighting factors.']
  rule_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive business name of the allocation rule used for identification and reporting.']
  rule_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the allocation rule by the type of financial element being allocated (cost, revenue, expense, premium, claim, administrative, medical, overhead, shared service, or intercompany).']
  source_cost_center varchar [note: 'The originating cost center from which costs or revenues are being allocated.']
  source_gl_account varchar [note: 'The general ledger account number from which the allocation originates.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The name or identifier of the source system from which this allocation rule was created or imported (e.g., SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Financials).']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of this allocation rule in the source system.']
  sox_control_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this allocation rule is subject to SOX internal controls and requires enhanced documentation and approval.']
  status varchar [note: 'The current lifecycle status of the allocation rule (active, inactive, pending, suspended, retired, draft, or under review).']
  statutory_filing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether allocations generated by this rule are included in statutory financial filings with state insurance departments.']
  target_dimension_type varchar [note: 'The type of financial dimension to which costs or revenues are allocated (cost center, department, line of business, product, geography, legal entity, business unit, service line, plan type, or network type).']
  version_number varchar [note: 'The version number of this allocation rule used to track changes and maintain audit history.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'The user identifier or name of the person who created this allocation rule.']

  Note: 'Reference definition of rules for allocating costs or revenues across financial dimensions.'
}

Table finance.cost_center_contract_allocation {
  allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the cost_center_contract_allocation association']
  contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the contract whose costs are being allocated']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the cost center receiving allocated contract costs']
  allocation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Calculated dollar amount of contract costs allocated to this cost center based on allocation percentage and total contract value']
  allocation_method varchar [note: 'Method used to determine the allocation percentage for this cost center (e.g., DIRECT assignment, PROPORTIONAL by revenue, HEADCOUNT-based, REVENUE-based, CUSTOM formula)']
  allocation_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes explaining the business rationale for this specific allocation percentage or method']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of contract costs allocated to this specific cost center. Must sum to 100% across all cost centers for a given contract.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this allocation record indicating whether it is actively used in financial reporting']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was created in the system']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this cost center allocation becomes effective for financial reporting']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when this cost center allocation ends or is superseded by a new allocation structure']
  last_modified_by varchar [note: 'User ID or name of the finance analyst who last modified this allocation record']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was last modified']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User ID or name of the finance analyst who created this allocation record']

  Note: 'This association product represents the financial allocation relationship between cost centers and contracts. It captures how contract costs are distributed across multiple organizational cost centers for P&L reporting and financial performance tracking. Each record links one cost center to one contract with allocation percentages and methods that exist only in the context of this financial distribution.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, provider and vendor contracts frequently span multiple organizational cost centers (regions, lines of business, departments) for financial reporting purposes. Finance teams actively manage allocation rules that distribute contract costs across cost centers using specific percentages and methods. This is an operational financial management process where allocation records are created, updated, and tracked over time with specific effective dates and allocation methods.'
}

Table finance.budget_allocation {
  budget_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the budget_allocation association']
  budget_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the budget record from which funds are allocated']
  program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the program receiving the budget allocation']
  allocated_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The specific dollar amount allocated from this budget to this program. This is relationship-specific data identified in the detection phase.']
  allocation_date date [note: 'The date when this budget allocation was made or approved. This is relationship-specific data identified in the detection phase.']
  allocation_type varchar [note: 'The type or category of this allocation (e.g., initial, supplemental, reallocation, adjustment).']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'The approval status of this specific budget allocation to the program. This is relationship-specific data identified in the detection phase.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was created in the system.']
  fiscal_year varchar [note: 'The fiscal year for which this budget allocation applies. This is relationship-specific data identified in the detection phase.']
  modified_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was last modified.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Additional notes or comments about this specific budget allocation to the program.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the allocation of budget amounts to specific programs. It captures the financial planning and tracking relationship between budgets and programs, recording how much of each budget is allocated to each program, when the allocation was made, and its approval status. Each record links one budget to one program with attributes that exist only in the context of this allocation relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance operations, a single budget line (e.g., Medical Management Operating Budget) is routinely allocated across multiple programs (Diabetes Management, COPD Care, Preventive Wellness), and conversely, a single program typically receives funding from multiple budget sources (operating budget, medical expense budget, administrative budget, grant funding). Finance actively manages these allocations as discrete records with specific amounts, approval workflows, and fiscal year tracking.'
}

  related_incident_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of any security incident, breach, or compliance violation that prompted this risk assessment.']

  remediation_target_date date [note: 'Target date for completing risk remediation activities.']

  review_date date [note: 'Date when the risk assessment findings were formally reviewed by management or compliance committee.']
  risk_appetite_alignment varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the identified risk level aligns with the organization\'s defined risk appetite and tolerance.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the overall risk level based on the risk score and impact analysis.']
  risk_owner varchar [note: 'Individual assigned ownership and accountability for managing the identified risks.']
  risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Calculated overall risk score for the assessment, typically on a scale of 0-100, representing the aggregate risk level identified.']

  scope_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the scope of the risk assessment, including systems, processes, departments, and data assets covered.']
  start_date date [note: 'Actual date when the risk assessment activities commenced.']
  third_party_assessor varchar [note: 'Name of external consulting firm or auditor engaged to conduct or validate the risk assessment.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version number of the risk assessment document, used to track revisions and updates.']

  Note: 'Periodic risk assessments of PHI handling processes, capturing assessment ID, scope, risk score, identified threats, and mitigation recommendations.'
}

  approval_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the compliance review for this asset-policy combination. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']
  compliance_review_date date [note: 'Date when the compliance review was conducted for this asset-policy combination. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']
  exception_granted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a compliance exception was granted for this asset-policy combination. Explicitly identified in detection phase.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the compliance review relationship between compliance policies and marketing assets. It captures the regulatory review and approval process required before marketing materials can be used in campaigns. Each record links one compliance policy to one marketing asset with review tracking attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory assessment.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, marketing assets must undergo compliance review against multiple regulatory policies (HIPAA privacy rules, CMS marketing guidelines, state-specific insurance advertising regulations, ADA accessibility standards). Each asset-policy combination requires independent review tracking because a single asset may be compliant with HIPAA but non-compliant with a specific state regulation, or may receive an exception for one policy but not another. The compliance team actively manages these reviews as operational records with review dates, reviewer assignments, approval statuses, and exception grants.'
}

Table marketing.campaign_enrollment {

  enrollment_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this enrollment record was created in the system']
  enrollment_date date [note: 'Date when the member risk profile was enrolled into the campaign, explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data']
  enrollment_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this enrollment record was last updated']
  outreach_priority_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Calculated priority score for outreach sequencing, determining the order in which enrolled members should be contacted, explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data']

  Note: 'This association product represents the enrollment of a member risk profile into a marketing campaign. Each record links one member risk profile to one campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this enrollment relationship.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, member risk profiles are actively enrolled into multiple marketing campaigns simultaneously (e.g., care gap closure, wellness programs, disease management outreach), and each campaign targets multiple member risk profiles based on risk stratification criteria. Campaign enrollment is an operational business process managed by marketing teams who create enrollment records, track member responses, prioritize outreach sequences, and document eligibility reasoning for each member-campaign combination.'
}

Table government.benefit_eligibility_rule {
  benefit_eligibility_rule_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the benefit_eligibility_rule association']
  benefit_design_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the government benefit design configuration']
  eligibility_rule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the eligibility rule being applied to this benefit design']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date-time when this benefit-eligibility rule assignment was created']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this eligibility rule becomes active for this specific benefit design, may differ from the rule\'s global effective date']
  override_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rule assignment overrides default eligibility logic or other rules for this benefit design']
  rule_priority varchar [note: 'Numeric priority for evaluating this rule within the context of this specific benefit design, overrides the rule\'s default priority when multiple rules apply to the same design']
  status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this rule assignment for this benefit design']
  termination_date date [note: 'Date when this eligibility rule is no longer applied to this benefit design, may differ from the rule\'s global expiration date']
  updated_by varchar [note: 'User or process identifier that performed the last update to this assignment']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date-time of the most recent modification to this assignment']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or process identifier that created this assignment']

  Note: 'This association product represents the configuration relationship between benefit designs and eligibility rules in government health insurance programs. It captures which eligibility rules are applied to each benefit design, with rule-specific precedence, effective dates, and override capabilities. Each record links one benefit design to one eligibility rule with attributes that govern how that rule is evaluated for that specific benefit plan.. Existence Justification: In government health insurance programs, a single benefit design (e.g., Medicare Advantage plan) must apply multiple eligibility rules simultaneously (age 65+, ESRD eligibility, disability status, residency requirements, SNP criteria). Conversely, the same eligibility rule (e.g., age 65+ for Medicare) is reused across hundreds of different benefit designs. Product configuration teams actively manage these rule assignments with design-specific effective dates, rule precedence, and override flags.'
}

Table government.contract_sla {
  contract_sla_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the contract_sla association']
  program_provider_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the government program provider contract']
  sla_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the SLA definition']
  actual_performance_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Measured actual performance for this contract-SLA in the most recent measurement period (e.g., 98.5% uptime, 95% claims processed within target).']
  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Current compliance status of this SLA for this contract based on most recent measurement period.']
  contract_specific_target decimal(5,2) [note: 'Contract-negotiated target that may differ from the standard SLA target (e.g., contract requires 99% uptime vs standard 98%).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this contract-SLA association record was created in the system.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this specific SLA becomes effective for this contract. May differ from contract effective date if SLAs are added mid-contract.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this SLA obligation expires or is superseded for this contract.']
  last_measurement_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent SLA compliance measurement for this contract.']
  measurement_period varchar [note: 'Time period over which SLA compliance is measured for this contract (e.g., monthly, quarterly, rolling 30-day).']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this contract-SLA association record.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next SLA performance review for this contract.']
  penalties_assessed_ytd decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total penalties assessed for this contract-SLA combination in the current calendar or contract year.']
  penalty_amount decimal(12,2) [note: 'Penalty amount specific to this contract-SLA combination, which may differ from the standard SLA penalty based on contract negotiation or contract size.']
  penalty_currency varchar [note: 'Currency code for the penalty amount, typically USD for US government programs.']
  reporting_contact_email varchar [note: 'Email address of the SLA reporting contact for this contract.']
  reporting_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the person responsible for SLA reporting for this specific contract.']
  status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this SLA obligation for this contract (active, suspended due to force majeure, waived by amendment, terminated).']
  waiver_reason varchar [note: 'Business reason if this SLA has been waived for this contract (e.g., system migration, natural disaster, contract amendment).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Service Level Agreement commitment between a government program provider contract and a specific SLA definition. It captures the contractual performance obligations, measurement periods, compliance tracking, and penalty enforcement for each contract-SLA combination. Each record links one program_provider_contract to one sla with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual commitment.. Existence Justification: In health insurance payer operations, government program provider contracts (Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care) include multiple distinct SLA obligations covering different service areas (claims processing turnaround, prior authorization response time, member access standards, grievance resolution, provider directory accuracy). Each SLA is a standardized template that applies to multiple contracts across the provider network. Network operations and contract management teams actively track compliance, measure performance, assess penalties, and report on each contract-SLA combination as a managed business entity.'
}
